Import weather data from Excel

Source: R/ImportWeather.R
ImportWeather.Rd

Imports weather data from an Excel workbook where individual worksheets contain data for separate years. Only worksheets required to cover the requested date range are imported. The resulting data are combined, filtered to the requested dates, and converted to long format.

The Excel workbook is expected to contain the following columns: `date`, `DOY`, `Temperature deg C`, `Air temp`, `Temp diff`, `Rainfall`, `Soil 15cm`, `Soil 45cm`, `Average Wind`, `RH`, `Leaf`, and `Lite totals`.

Worksheet names are expected to contain the four-digit year, for example `"2023"`, `"2024"`, and `"2025"`.

Usage

ImportWeather(file, start_date = "2013-01-01", end_date = Sys.Date())

Arguments

file

Character string. Path to the Excel workbook containing the weather data.

start_date

Start date of the period to import. Either a `Date` object or a character string that can be converted to a date using `as.Date()`, e.g. `"2023-01-01"`.

end_date

End date of the period to import. Either a `Date` object or a character string that can be converted to a date using `as.Date()`, e.g. `"2025-12-31"`.

Value

A tibble in long format with four columns:

date

Observation date.

DOY

Day of year.

variable

Weather variable measured.

value

Observed value.

Details

Only worksheets corresponding to years between `start_date` and `end_date` are read. For example, a request from `"2023-06-01"` to `"2025-04-30"` will attempt to read the 2023, 2024 and 2025 worksheets.

After the worksheets have been combined, observations outside the requested date range are removed.

Author

Gareth Burns

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
weather <- import_weather(
  file = "weather.xlsx",
  start_date = "2022-01-01",
  end_date = "2025-12-31"
)

weather
} # }
